objects.description: Abstract output stream interface used by OTS to write sanitized OpenType data while maintaining a running checksum. Subclasses must implement size(), WriteRaw(), Seek(), and Tell(). Provides helpers for writing integer types with network byte order and padding.
Customization and entry point class for running the OTS sanitizer. Provides Process() to sanitize an input font to an OTSStream, and virtual hooks for logging and per-table action decisions.
Concrete OTSStream that writes into a caller-provided fixed-size memory buffer. Fails writes that would exceed the buffer size. Maintains an internal offset and supports seeking within bounds.
Resizable memory-backed OTSStream implementation. Starts with an initial capacity and doubles up to a specified limit when more space is required by writes. Exposes the internal buffer via get().
Enumeration controlling how OTS handles individual font tables during processing: default behavior, sanitize, passthrough, drop, or soft-sanitize (don’t fail overall if table sanitization fails).

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::size
functions.description: Returns the stream’s capacity/size as reported by the concrete OTSStream implementation. Pure virtual; implemented by derived classes such as MemoryStream and ExpandingMemoryStream.
requirements: Must be called on a valid instance of a concrete subclass (OTSStream is abstract).
No side effects; safe to call anytime the stream object is valid.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteRaw
functions.signature: virtual bool ots::OTSStream::WriteRaw(const void *data, size_t length) = 0;
functions.description: Low-level write used by OTSStream to actually output bytes. Implementations must perform the write without modifying checksum state; OTSStream::Write handles checksum accumulation and then calls WriteRaw.
requirements: Must be called on a valid instance of a concrete subclass (pure virtual).
data must point to at least length bytes if length > 0.
Return true on complete write, false on failure (caller should not assume partial success).
Implementations must not alter OTSStream::chksum_ (checksum is handled by Write).

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::Write
functions.description: Writes length bytes from data to the stream and updates the running 32-bit checksum (sum of big-endian 32-bit words with final partial aligned as documented in code). Delegates the actual output to WriteRaw.
requirements: data must point to at least length bytes; undefined behavior if data is null and length > 0.
length must be non-zero; if length == 0 the function returns false and performs no write.
The underlying WriteRaw must be functional; Write returns false if WriteRaw returns false.
Callers should not rely on atomicity: on failure, some bytes may have already been written by WriteRaw.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::Seek
functions.description: Moves the stream’s write/read position to position. Semantics depend on the concrete stream implementation.
requirements: Must be called on a valid instance of a concrete subclass (pure virtual).
position must be within the valid range for the concrete stream (see derived classes).
Return true on success, false if the position is invalid or unsupported.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current stream position (offset).
requirements: Must be called on a valid instance of a concrete subclass (pure virtual).
No side effects; callable at any time the stream is valid.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::Pad
functions.description: Writes bytes zero bytes to the stream (padding) using 32-bit chunks where possible, then single bytes, updating the checksum accordingly.
requirements: bytes is the number of zero bytes to write; may be zero (returns true with no write).
Underlying Write must succeed for all emitted chunks; returns false on the first failure.
May partially write before failing; caller must handle partial output.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteU8
functions.description: Writes an 8-bit unsigned integer to the stream without byte-order conversion.
requirements: No special range requirements beyond uint8_t (0..255).
Returns false if the underlying Write fails (e.g., out of space).

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteU16
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit unsigned integer to the stream in network/big-endian order.
requirements: Input v is host-endian; function converts to big-endian.
Returns false if the underlying Write fails.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteS16
functions.description: Writes a 16-bit signed integer to the stream in network/big-endian order.
requirements: Input v is host-endian; function converts to big-endian.
Returns false if the underlying Write fails.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteU24
functions.description: Writes a 24-bit unsigned integer (lower 24 bits of v) to the stream in network/big-endian order.
requirements: Only the least significant 24 bits of v are written; callers should ensure v fits in 24 bits to avoid truncation.
Returns false if the underlying Write fails.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteU32
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit unsigned integer to the stream in network/big-endian order.
requirements: Input v is host-endian; function converts to big-endian.
Returns false if the underlying Write fails.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteS32
functions.description: Writes a 32-bit signed integer to the stream in network/big-endian order.
requirements: Input v is host-endian; function converts to big-endian.
Returns false if the underlying Write fails.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::WriteR64
functions.description: Writes a 64-bit value to the stream exactly as provided (no byte-order conversion). Intended for raw 64-bit fields that are already in desired endianness.
requirements: Caller is responsible for endianness; value is written as-is.
Returns false if the underlying Write fails.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::ResetChecksum
functions.description: Resets the running checksum accumulator to zero. Asserts that the current position is 4-byte aligned (Tell() & 3 == 0).
requirements: Must only be called when Tell() is 4-byte aligned; otherwise the internal assert will fail in debug builds.
Has no effect on stream position or contents.

functions.name: ots::OTSStream::chksum
functions.description: Returns the current accumulated checksum value maintained by OTSStream::Write and related writes.
requirements: Call after writes to inspect the checksum state; read-only and side-effect free.

functions.name: ots::OTSContext::Process
functions.signature: bool ots::OTSContext::Process(OTSStream *output, const uint8_t *input, size_t length, uint32_t index = static_cast<uint32_t>(-1));
functions.description: Sanitizes an OpenType font (or collection) from the given input buffer and writes the sanitized result to output. On failure, partial output may have been written. If input is a font collection and index is specified, the corresponding font is returned; otherwise, the whole collection is processed.
requirements: output must be a valid, writable OTSStream instance.
input must point to at least length bytes of the font data; length must reflect the input size.
Caller must handle the boolean return value: false indicates sanitization failed and partial output may exist and must not be used as a valid font.
index is used only for font collections; ignored for non-collection fonts.

functions.name: ots::OTSContext::Message
functions.signature: virtual void ots::OTSContext::Message(int level, const char *format, ...) MSGFUNC_FMT_ATTR;
functions.description: Callback for reporting messages during processing. level indicates severity (0: error, 1: warning). format follows printf-style formatting, with variadic arguments.
requirements: Implementations should accept printf-style format and arguments consistent with the format string.
level values 0 and 1 are defined; other values may be ignored or treated as implementation-defined.
Must be callable from OTS processing threads/context; implementation should be reentrant or thread-safe if used concurrently.

functions.name: ots::OTSContext::GetTableAction
functions.description: Decides how OTS should handle a specific font table identified by tag (use OTS_TAG to build tags). Default returns TABLE_ACTION_DEFAULT.
requirements: tag must be a 4-byte OpenType table tag encoded via OTS_TAG or equivalent.
Implementations should return one of the TableAction enum values to guide processing.

functions.name: ots::MemoryStream::MemoryStream
functions.description: Constructs a fixed-size memory-backed stream over the buffer [ptr, ptr+length). Writes that exceed length or overflow arithmetic fail.
requirements: ptr must point to a writable buffer of at least length bytes that remains valid for the lifetime of the MemoryStream.
length defines the maximum writable size; no reallocation occurs.
Behavior is undefined if ptr is null and length > 0.

functions.name: ots::MemoryStream::size
functions.description: Returns the total capacity (length) of the underlying fixed buffer.
requirements: Object must be a valid MemoryStream instance.

functions.name: ots::MemoryStream::WriteRaw
functions.signature: bool ots::MemoryStream::WriteRaw(const void *data, size_t length) override;
functions.description: Writes length bytes from data into the fixed buffer at the current offset. Fails if the write would exceed the buffer or if size arithmetic would overflow. Advances the offset on success.
requirements: data must point to at least length bytes.
Write fails (returns false) if off_ + length > length_ or if size_t overflow would occur.
On success, exactly length bytes are written; on failure, no bytes are written.

functions.name: ots::MemoryStream::Seek
functions.description: Sets the current position to position within the fixed buffer.
requirements: position must be >= 0 and <= length_.
Returns false if position is out of range; does not change the offset in that case.

functions.name: ots::MemoryStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current position within the buffer.
requirements: Object must be a valid MemoryStream instance.

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::ExpandingMemoryStream
functions.description: Constructs a growable memory-backed stream with an initial allocation of initial bytes and a maximum capacity limit. The buffer grows geometrically on demand up to limit.
requirements: initial bytes are allocated immediately; allocation must succeed (otherwise construction throws in standard C++ new).
limit defines the maximum capacity; writes beyond limit will fail.
For predictable behavior, initial should be <= limit (not enforced in code but larger initial than limit prevents growth and may cause immediate failures for larger writes).

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::~ExpandingMemoryStream
functions.description: Destructor; releases the allocated buffer.
requirements: Do not use the stream after destruction.
No special requirements for callers beyond normal C++ object lifetime management.

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal buffer. Useful for accessing the accumulated bytes after writing.
requirements: Pointer remains valid until the stream is destroyed or reallocated by further writes; subsequent writes may reallocate and invalidate previously obtained pointers.
Caller is responsible for tracking the valid written length via stream position or external bookkeeping (no length is returned by get).

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::size
functions.description: Returns the maximum capacity (limit) of the expanding stream, not the current used size.
requirements: Object must be a valid ExpandingMemoryStream instance.
Note: This reports the limit, not the current write position or current allocated length.

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::WriteRaw
functions.description: Writes length bytes to the stream, expanding the internal buffer geometrically as needed up to the configured limit. On success, advances the offset by length. Fails if the write would exceed the limit or if size arithmetic overflows.
requirements: data must point to at least length bytes.
If off_ + length exceeds current allocation, the stream attempts to grow up to limit_. If already at limit_ and more space is needed, returns false.
Handles size_t overflow guards; returns false if (off_ + length) would overflow size_t.
On success, exactly length bytes are written and the offset advances by length.

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::Seek
functions.description: Sets the current position within the currently allocated buffer (not beyond the current allocation length).
requirements: position must be >= 0 and <= current allocated length (length_).
Returns false if position is out of range; does not change the offset in that case.

functions.name: ots::ExpandingMemoryStream::Tell
functions.description: Returns the current position (offset) within the buffer.
requirements: Object must be a valid ExpandingMemoryStream instance.

data_types.description: A byte buffer with no required structure or encoding. May contain any sequence of bytes including nulls and non-UTF-8 data. Used when functions write raw payloads to streams without interpreting content.
A generic human-readable string intended for textual messages. Typically UTF-8 but not strictly enforced; passed to printf-style "%s" consumers.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# Generator for a generic text string meant for printf("%s") usage.
# The fuzzer stub pulls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and passes it as a C-string.
# Our buffer should therefore contain a plausible, interesting NUL-terminated
# string payload. AFL-style harnesses often split one input buffer across
# multiple FUZZ_PARAM_* calls. We'll encode a single logical string that
# parsers can slice from. Keep under 4096 bytes.

ASCII_PRINTABLE = [
    *(range(0x20, 0x7f))  # space to tilde
]

COMMON_PREFIXES = [
    "", "Error: ", "Warning: ", "Info: ",
    "[OTS] ", "<debug> ", "msg:",
]

# Include diverse unicode samples that still make sense as UTF-8 and printf %s
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "こんにちは",  # Japanese
    "Привет",     # Russian
    "مرحبا",      # Arabic
    "你好",        # Chinese
    "🙂😀🙃",      # Emoji
    "Ångström",   # Latin extended
]

EDGE_CASES = [
    "",  # empty string
    " ",
    "\t",
    "\n",
    "\r\n",
    "%",           # percent by itself
    "%%",          # escaped percent-like content
    "%s",          # would be safe because format is fixed, but interesting content
    "%9999999s",   # large width
    "%.0s",        # precision zero
    "%-20s",       # left-justify
    "{json:false}",
    "(null)",
    "A" * 1024,    # long but within cap
]

WORDS = [
    "font", "glyph", "table", "cmap", "head", "name", "kern", "GSUB",
    "GPOS", "OTF", "TTF", "COLR", "CPAL", "CFF", "sanitizer", "checksum",
    "stream", "write", "seek", "tell", "pad", "u16", "u32",
]

SEPARATORS = [" ", "-", "_", ":", ";", ", ", "|", "/", "::", "#"]


def _rand_choice(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _build_interesting_text(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Occasionally return a predefined edge case
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return _rand_choice(rng, EDGE_CASES)

    parts = []
    # Optional prefix
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, COMMON_PREFIXES))

    # Mix words with separators
    n_words = rng.randint(1, 10)
    for i in range(n_words):
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, UNICODE_SAMPLES))
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, WORDS))
        if i != n_words - 1:
            parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, SEPARATORS))

    # Optional trailing punctuation or newline patterns
    tail_opts = ["", "\n", "\r\n", "...", "!", "?", " \n"]
    parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, tail_opts))

    s = "".join(parts)

    # Occasionally include percent signs inside but they are just data; format is fixed to "%s"
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        insert_pos = rng.randrange(0, len(s) + 1)
        s = s[:insert_pos] + (" %" * rng.randint(1, 5)) + s[insert_pos:]

    # Cap size to remain under overall limit when encoded and NUL-terminated
    return s[:3500]


def _encode_c_string(text: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8; ensure no embedded NUL so C "%s" prints full string
    # If there are NULs, replace them with visible \x00-like sequence
    text = text.replace("\x00", "<NUL>")
    data = text.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    return data + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build one or multiple C-strings concatenated, so harnesses that draw
    # multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR slices have material to consume. We'll pack:
    # [count][len1][str1\0][len2][str2\0]... in a simple self-describing blob,
    # but many fuzzers just pass raw; including lengths first keeps it robust if
    # the harness interprets size, and harmless if not (they just become part of the string).

    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    chunks = []

    # Header: magic + count
    magic = b"OTSMSG\x01"  # recognizable prefix
    chunks.append(magic)
    chunks.append(struct.pack("<I", count))

    for _ in range(count):
        s = _build_interesting_text(rng)
        b = _encode_c_string(s)
        chunks.append(struct.pack("<I", len(b)))
        chunks.append(b)

    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    # Ensure max size <= 4096
    return blob[:4096]
